title: Extraction and characterization of biodegradable bioplastic from the red seaweed Gelidium sesquipedale and its application for fresh‐cut apple preservation
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

This study evaluated the extraction, macromolecular characterization, and active packaging application of polysaccharides derived from the red seaweed Gelidium sesquipedale for fresh-cut apple preservation.

RESULTS

Thermo-alkaline extraction (20 g kg−1 NaOH, 60 °C), yielded 380 g kg−1 of an agarose rich galactan fraction. High-performance liquid chromatography–refractive index detection confirmed high d-galactose (684 ± 12 g kg−1) and 3,6-anhydro-l-galactose (261 ± 8 g kg−1) contents, validating successful alkali-induced desulfation down to 5.2 g kg−1 sulfates. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy further confirmed the characteristic agarobiose repeating backbone. The formulated active film plasticized with 100 g kg−1 glycerol exhibited robust mechanical integrity and a favorable water vapor permeability (1.75 × 10−6g m−1 s−1 Pa−1). When evaluated as an active insert liner for the preservation of fresh-cut apples over 12 days at 4 °C, the film significantly reduced cumulative weight loss (37.6 vs 133.2 g kg−1 for control) and maintained headspace gas equilibrium. Furthermore, the active packaging effectively inhibited polyphenol oxidase activity by 53.8%, reduced ascorbic acid degradation by 41.2%, and preserved fresh-cut apple color by retarding enzymatic browning.

CONCLUSION

Gelidium sesquipedale galactans demonstrate high performance as a sustainable active packaging matrix, providing an effective, clean-label strategy to inhibit postharvest enzymatic browning and extend fresh-cut produce shelf life. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
